On the Kuerig 2.0 units this item allows the bottom pin to puncture the filter on occasion releasing grounds into the coffee.  It doesn't do it every time but enough to be annoying. Leaves me starving for a stronger cup of coffee and cleaning up the mess.

6/7/2017 Update: I tried taking the spring out of the spring by pressing down on it, so much so that it actually snapped out of the holder. The little piece that held the spring in place snapped off. However; now that the spring is less springy, I can put more coffee in the filter, I even pack in down a little, and I get my stronger cup of coffee that I've been starving for. So far, no exploded filters like I had before the surgery.

I would give this product 5 stars if their packaging was more eco-friendly.  I love the product itself.  Of all the keurig alternatives I have tried, this one makes a great cup of my choice of coffee, and is easiest to clean without getting coffee grounds in my plumbing.  However, the largest quantity available (50 count) seems to be packaged in the same amount of plastic I'm trying to avoid throwing away.  When you buy 200, you receive 4 heavy plastic containers of 50 perfect pods (gah!). What's the point?

BEST refillable I've found...

BEST refillable I've found...all others leak grounds into coffee. A friend gave me one of these and a few papers, along with a couple of filters, and I've ordered and returned three other's that were screened, one-supposedly gold but actually had grey mesh...I finally decided to order just another "purple-perfect" [my nick-name for the cups]. I realized I'd finally found a way to use my coffee, and recycle the papers. And, in a pinch, I rinsed one of these out while waiting for my new box to arrive, and it was still MUCH better than any throwaway pod I've tried so far! plan on sticking with this system.

This item is ALMOST perfect. It allows you to use ANY coffee or tea without the high price of the programmed kcup dispenser. You use the filter with the reusable EZ kcup dispenser. After use you dispose of the paper EZ
filter which holds the grains and simply rinse and hang up the reusable dispenser to drip dry. The plastic kcup dispenser can be immediately reused however a new filter sticks to the wet surface so it is good to have a couple on hand if you'll be making several cups back to back. The filters will actually work with any of the various kcup dispensers available. It also means that with each cup of coffee you are not throwing a non- biodegradable plastic kcup into a landfill. The filters do the job well as long as the is not overfilled and the paper lid is centered over the coffee grains. This item would be perfect if it came in a more biologically friendly easy to use dispenser and if the price was more reasonable. $12.50 for 200 tiny tissue paper filters is high by any standard. Otherwise this coffee filter which allows the user to save money on coffee, allows the use of any coffee or tea even if not available as a kcup, helps save the environment, and bypass the ridiculous restrictions of the 2.0 machine is perfect product.
